correctness.rationale: Generator first-step identities and the explicit two-eigenvalue density formula yield the entire theorem. When storage reaction is smaller, both density coefficients are positive and the density ratio is strictly convex, initially decreasing and ultimately increasing, with a single positive derivative crossover. A positive or zero exact terminal gap gives the unique cumulative sign reversal or all-finite-horizon deficit. A shared-clock coupling establishes strict dominance for storage reaction at least as fast as mobile reaction. Monotone storage killing and eigenvalue/Taylor expansions prove monotonicity and endpoint scales. Independent standard-library 4-state uniformization and 1200 rational first-step checks contributed to 7146 finite assertions. Risks: asymptotics assume fixed positive remaining rates; finite checker is not infinite proof.

value.rationale: A physically motivated finite-observation paradox is resolved exactly: inert storage delays reaction without raising eventual reaction, slow reactive storage crosses from apparent loss to eventual gain exactly once, and equally fast storage raises reaction at every deadline. Complete regime boundaries and asymptotic crossover scales supply quantitative time-horizon tests for interpreting idealized transient-storage measurements. This is not merely a parameter substitution or a new numerical tabulation and it does not assert unvalidated field performance.
